history.alt_text: Two identical modular server drive caddies side-by-side on a wooden bench, one open and the other sealed with a brass lock.
history.caption: When a vendor splits a single repository into two shipping builds, a self-hosted server becomes an ongoing audit of which features made the cut.
history.title: Bitwarden dual build license split

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly resting on a home office workbench. A split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast: two identical brushed metal server drive caddies side-by-side. The left caddy is open and unlatched; the right caddy is sealed shut with an integrated heavy brass lock mechanism. Clean hard edges on weathered painted wood, single directional light throwing long cast shadows from the left. Matte muted palette of slate grey, bone white, and warm brass. Generous negative space.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, watermarks, gibberish, ui, labels, glowing, neon, spheres, cubes, loose scraps
rationale: The story is about a structural change in how software is packaged and licensed (two builds from one source, one locked down). Component assembly perfectly captures this systemic, modular shift by showing two identical server parts with different access states on a physical workbench.
subject: two identical modular server drive caddies side-by-side, one locked with a brass mechanism
core_thesis: The free self-hosted build is now a shipping decision the vendor owns, so the cost of a license split lands as an audit of every device you enrolled rather than as a price you can see coming.
core_conflict: Open-source self-hosting promise vs. vendor-controlled feature gating and licensing splits
